records.Name: SNAP (Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program)
records.Agency__c: Indiana FSSA — Division of Family Resources
records.Description__c: Monthly food benefits loaded onto an EBT card. Survivors who left with little or no food security qualify in nearly every case.
records.Eligibility_Notes__c: Income under ~130% of federal poverty level. Household size matters — single survivor much easier than multi-person household. Indiana ACP enrollees can apply confidentially.
records.Internal_Notes__c: Typical approval timeline: 7-30 days. Expedited SNAP available within 7 days for very-low-income households. We can help fill out the application; the survivor needs ID and proof of income/expenses.

records.Name: TANF (Temporary Assistance for Needy Families)
records.Agency__c: Indiana FSSA — Division of Family Resources
records.Description__c: Cash assistance for families with children. Modest monthly amount but unlocks other benefits and is a stepping stone to work-readiness programs.
records.Eligibility_Notes__c: Must have a dependent child. Income under ~30% FPL. Time-limited (60-month lifetime federal cap). Work participation requirement after initial enrollment.
records.Internal_Notes__c: Same application as SNAP. Often paired. The work-participation requirement can be challenging — we coordinate with WorkOne for compliance.

records.Name: WIC (Women, Infants, and Children)
records.Description__c: Nutrition support for pregnant/postpartum survivors and children under 5. Specific food packages plus nutrition counseling.
records.Eligibility_Notes__c: Pregnant, breastfeeding, or postpartum (up to 6 months), or have a child under 5. Income up to 185% FPL. Categorically eligible if already on SNAP/TANF/Medicaid.
records.Internal_Notes__c: Walk-in appointments at the Hancock County office. Bring ID, proof of pregnancy or child's birth, proof of income.

records.Name: Indiana Medicaid / HIP 2.0
records.Agency__c: Indiana FSSA — Office of Medicaid Policy and Planning
records.Description__c: Free or very-low-cost health coverage. Hoosier Healthwise (children/pregnant), HIP 2.0 (adults), Hoosier Care Connect (aged/disabled).
records.Eligibility_Notes__c: Income thresholds vary by program. HIP 2.0 covers adults up to 138% FPL. Most survivors qualify post-separation due to income drop.
records.Internal_Notes__c: Apply alongside SNAP/TANF — same application. Coverage retroactive 3 months in some cases.

records.Name: Section 8 Housing Choice Voucher
records.Agency__c: HUD via Indianapolis HA / Indiana HA
records.Description__c: Federal rental assistance — pay 30% of income, government pays the rest. Use at participating landlords.
records.Eligibility_Notes__c: Income under 50% area median. CRITICAL: waiting lists are 2-5+ years in Indiana. DV survivors qualify for preference category in most PHAs.
records.Internal_Notes__c: Apply early. DV preference letter from SFTS shortens wait. Indianapolis HA opens lists periodically — monitor housing.in.gov.

records.Name: LIHEAP (Low-Income Home Energy Assistance)
records.Description__c: Help with heating/cooling bills. Winter EAP credits utility account; summer cooling assistance June-September.
records.Eligibility_Notes__c: Income up to 60% state median income. Open enrollment Nov-May for winter EAP.
records.Internal_Notes__c: Hancock County office handles intake. Bring utility bills, ID, proof of income for all household members.

records.Name: Indiana Emergency Rental Assistance
records.Description__c: One-time assistance with rent + utilities for households at risk of housing instability.
records.Eligibility_Notes__c: Income under 80% area median, demonstrated housing instability, COVID-19-related or general hardship. Program availability varies by year.
records.Internal_Notes__c: Funding cycles open and close — check current availability before applying. We've had good luck pairing with LIHEAP applications.

records.Name: Indiana Unemployment Insurance
records.Description__c: Weekly cash benefit for survivors who lost employment through no fault of their own. DV-related job loss qualifies in Indiana.
records.Eligibility_Notes__c: Must have worked 2 of last 5 quarters. Indiana recognizes DV-induced separation as good-cause unemployment.
records.Internal_Notes__c: Survivor must request DV exemption EXPLICITLY when filing — otherwise the system may flag voluntary quit. We can help draft the explanation.

records.Name: SSDI / SSI
records.Description__c: Federal disability income for survivors with physical or mental health conditions limiting work capacity. SSDI for those with work history; SSI for those without.
records.Eligibility_Notes__c: Disability determination required. PTSD, anxiety, and depression from DV are qualifying when documented and severe. Process is 3-24 months.
records.Internal_Notes__c: Get clinical documentation early. Indiana Legal Services has a disability-benefits practice that can take cases pro bono.

records.Name: WorkOne / Indiana Career Connect
records.Description__c: Job search assistance, resume writing, training programs, interview prep. WIOA-funded vocational training available.
records.Eligibility_Notes__c: Open to all job seekers. Priority for low-income / displaced workers / TANF recipients.
records.Internal_Notes__c: Hancock County WorkOne is in Greenfield. Walk-ins welcome. WIOA training scholarships pay for certified-trade programs (medical asst, IT cert, CDL, etc.).

records.Name: Indiana Legal Services (free legal aid)
records.Description__c: Free civil legal representation for low-income Hoosiers. DV / family law / housing / public benefits / consumer rights.
records.Eligibility_Notes__c: Income under 200% FPL. DV cases get priority. Accepts referrals from SFTS.
records.Internal_Notes__c: Don't promise representation — they accept based on intake panel review. But they often DO take DV cases. We've built a referral relationship with the Indianapolis office.

records.Name: VINE (Victim Information and Notification Everyday)
records.Description__c: Free automated notification when an offender's custody status changes (release from jail, transfer, court date).
records.Eligibility_Notes__c: Available to any victim. No income or eligibility requirements.
records.Internal_Notes__c: Register the survivor's number AND a backup number. Notifications via phone, text, and email. Critical for survivors whose abuser is incarcerated.

records.Name: Indiana Address Confidentiality Program (ACP)
records.Description__c: Substitute mailing address for survivors hiding from abusers. Mail forwarded to real address; abuser can't trace through public records.
records.Eligibility_Notes__c: Must be a victim of DV, stalking, sexual assault, or trafficking. Requires application + DV provider attestation (SFTS qualifies as attester).
records.Internal_Notes__c: We can attest to eligibility. 4-year enrollment, renewable. Crucial for survivors who must update DMV, voter registration, school records, etc.

records.Name: Crime Victim Compensation Fund
records.Description__c: Reimburses out-of-pocket victim expenses: medical, mental health counseling, funeral costs, lost wages, relocation. Up to $15K per claim.
records.Eligibility_Notes__c: Must have reported the crime to law enforcement. Application within 2 years of incident. Income not a barrier.
records.Internal_Notes__c: Often overlooked. Even survivors with insurance benefit — covers deductibles, co-pays, items insurance won't (relocation, counseling). We help compile the documentation.

records.Name: Indiana ID Replacement (BMV)
records.Description__c: Replacement driver's license or state ID when abuser kept or destroyed the survivor's documents.
records.Eligibility_Notes__c: Survivor must have proof of identity (birth cert, SSN card, or fallback documents). DV survivors qualify for fee waiver via attestation letter.
records.Internal_Notes__c: Often the FIRST task on a new case — without ID, nothing else can be applied for. SFTS issues fee-waiver attestation letters; survivor takes to a BMV branch.
